Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - recap & next steps

Sam — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same baseline and can make a pricing recommendation that fits your goals.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Workload: real-time chat assistant + batch nightly embedding jobs (search index updates).
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~250M tokens/day (peak bursts up to ~450M/day during promotional events).
- Latency SLO: 95th pct < 180ms for chat flows.
- Target unit economics: ~ $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens (target ideally near $1,000/1M).
- Budget range discussed: $60k — $150k / month depending on reserved capacity and SLA.
- Preference: would like reserved (Dedicated) capacity for predictable performance and data isolation.

Questions for you / next inputs we need to finalize a proposal:
1) Can you confirm typical concurrency (avg requests/sec) for chat flows and average prompt + completion length in tokens?
2) Nightly batch window / tolerable run-time for embeddings jobs?
3) Any hard restrictions on GPU vendor/type (e.g., must be A100)?

Next steps:
- Marcus will sketch expected throughput estimates (tokens/sec) for candidate configs (A100 vs H100, 4/8/16 GPU pools).
- Marissa will follow up with ballpark pricing and unit economics for the configurations that meet your targets.
- If the ballpark looks good, we'll set a technical scoping session to finalize kernel/quantization and an SOW.

Attaching the MAP you shared and our standard dedicated pricing workbook for internal reference.

Thanks — Vanessa

--

Hi all — jumping in with some engineering-level estimates and approach so pricing reflects expected unit economics. High-level guidance below; happy to walk through numbers on a call.

Assumptions used:
- Model: 70B decoder-only LLM (latency-sensitive chat).
- Batch-sizing for chat: effective tokens/batch ~1024 at steady state for continuous batching + KV cache reuse.
- Tokenization avg: 1 token ~= 4 characters (your ~400-token avg aligns).

Ballpark throughput by GPU type (in tokens/sec per GPU) @ target latency envelope (95p < 180ms):
- H100 (nvidia H100, optimized kernels): ~18k–24k tokens/sec per GPU (depending on batch/quantization).
- A100 (nvidia A100 80GB): ~10k–14k tokens/sec per GPU.

So recommended reserved pool sizing to hit steady-state 250M tokens/day (~2,893 tokens/sec average):
- 4x H100 -> ~72k – 96k tokens/sec total (well above steady-state; provides headroom for burst). 4x is likely overkill if budget-constrained.
- 2x H100 -> ~36k – 48k tokens/sec (still plenty of headroom).
- 8x A100 -> ~80k – 112k tokens/sec (comparable to 4x H100 but with different cost profile).

For your peak bursts (450M/day -> ~5,208 tokens/sec), even smaller configs cover peaks; the key is throughput under 95p latency. For predictable SLOs during highest peaks and aggressive batching for embeddings, we typically recommend 4–8 GPUs depending on whether you prioritize lower unit $/token (more GPUs amortize fixed infra) or lower absolute spend.

Notes on unit economics modeling:
- Tokens processed for embeddings batch can be scheduled to off-peak to reduce required peak capacity.
- Quantization & kernel choices materially affect throughput; our pricing workbook will model mixed precision and quantization options.

I attached a short workbook with the per-GPU throughput assumptions and a simple token-cost calc (see pricing-workbook-vanessa.xlsx).

—Marcus

Sam — thanks for the details. Based on Marcus's throughput estimates and your budget guidance, here are two ballpark committed-reserved configurations for Acme to consider. These are intended as starting points for your internal review (no contract yet).

Option A (cost-optimized): 8x A100 (80GB) reserved pool\- Expected steady throughput: ~80k–112k tokens/sec (covers steady-state + burst).\- Monthly committed price: $85,000 / month (reserved, 24/7 access)\- Modeled unit cost: ~$1,050 per 1M tokens (assumes typical batching and 70% utilization on chat + embeddings scheduled overnight).

Option B (performance-optimized): 4x H100 reserved pool\- Expected steady throughput: ~72k–96k tokens/sec (lower GPU count, higher per-GPU throughput).\- Monthly committed price: $120,000 / month (reserved, 24/7 access, includes higher-priority capacity and 99.9% latency SLA)\- Modeled unit cost: ~$920 per 1M tokens (better unit economics due to higher throughput per GPU and lower overall cluster overhead).

Notes / assumptions:
- Unit cost approximations include model inference runtime, reserved infra amortization, and standard support. They exclude optional add-ons (long-term log retention, custom evals).
- We assumed 250M tokens/day steady with 450M/day peak; if your true avg is lower, unit costs improve.
- If you want true best-effort lower $/1M, we can model a larger reserved pool to increase utilization but that raises committed spend.

Requested next steps:
1) Can you confirm which option aligns with procurement (Option A within their price preference; Option B exceeds the preferred ceiling but delivers better unit $/token)?
2) If you want Option B, we should schedule the scoping call to pin down quantization and operational SLOs so Marcus can finalize perf numbers for the SOW.

If helpful, we can also prepare a blended recommendation (e.g., 6x A100 or 3x H100) to land inside the $120k ceiling while getting improved unit economics.

Happy to jump on a 30 minute slot this week to review.

—Marissa
